back: On top of that / What's more
example: It's expensive. On top of that, it's badly located.

back: Furthermore / Moreover / In addition
example: Moreover, the costs are rising.

back: That said / Having said that
example: It's a great city. That said, it's very expensive.

back: However / Nevertheless / Nonetheless
example: The plan is risky. Nevertheless, it's worth trying.

front: to introduce a contrasting fact (two clauses)
back: whereas / while
example: He likes the city, whereas she prefers the countryside.

back: although / even though / despite + -ing
example: Despite having little experience, she got the job.

front: to admit a point before disagreeing
back: Admittedly / Granted
example: Granted, it's not perfect, but it works.

back: Consequently / As a result / Therefore
example: Sales fell; consequently, jobs were cut.

back: So / That's why / Which means
example: The trains were on strike, which meant we had to drive.

back: Owing to / Due to / In view of
example: Owing to the weather, the event was cancelled.

back: For instance / Take ... for example / such as
example: Take Denmark, for example.

back: In other words / That is to say
example: In other words, we're out of money.

back: Or rather / To be more precise
example: I'll finish it tomorrow - or rather, on Monday.

back: On the whole / By and large / Generally speaking
example: By and large, the feedback was positive.

front: to say something is true only partly
back: To some extent / Up to a point
example: I agree with you up to a point.

back: All in all / So, to sum up
example: All in all, it was a success.

back: In conclusion / To conclude
example: In conclusion, the evidence is clear.

front: to consider both sides before deciding
back: On balance
example: On balance, I think we should go ahead.

back: By the way / Speaking of which / Anyway
example: Speaking of which, did you see the game?

front: to return to the main topic
back: Anyway, getting back to... / Coming back to...
example: Coming back to your question...

front: to say what is true in reality, contrasting with appearance
back: In fact / Actually / As a matter of fact
example: As a matter of fact, I've never been there.

front: to express that something is surprising
back: Surprisingly / Believe it or not
example: Believe it or not, he agreed.

front: to express that something is not surprising
back: Unsurprisingly / Needless to say / Of course
example: Needless to say, we were exhausted.

back: Meanwhile / In the meantime
example: In the meantime, please wait here.

back: At any rate / In any case / Either way
example: Either way, we need to decide today.

front: to express a condition that everything depends on
back: provided that / as long as / assuming that
example: Assuming that the weather holds, we'll go.

back: so as to / in order to / with a view to + -ing
example: We met with a view to reaching a deal.

back: To be honest / Frankly / If you ask me
example: Frankly, I don't think it'll work.
